newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan vegoil imports seen falling on devaluation.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan vegoil imports seen falling on devaluation.

text.p: Pakistan's vegetable oil imports are likely to fall in 1996/97 (July-June) because of a rupee devaluation and other economic measures which will drive up prices and depress consumption, dealers said on Wednesday.
"I see a fall of 20 percent in vegoil imports for the next two months," dealer Saulat Khan told Reuters.
He said imports might then pick up slightly, but there would be an overall drop of 15 percent in the whole of 1996/97.

On Tuesday, the government devalued the rupee 7.86 percent against the dollar, imposed a two percent service charge on imports and added one percent to income tax under a tough economic stabilisation package it said had the approval of the International Monetary Fund.
"The first impact of the package and the devaluation was the scrapping of 9,000 tonnes of RBD palm oil bids by the Ghee Corp of Pakistan (GCP) on Tuesday," dealer Kamran Khan said.
The state-run Trading Corp of Pakistan, which buys vegoil for the GCP, scrapped its tender for 9,000 tonnes of palm oil on Tuesday without giving a reason.

"Vegoil processors, who are confused over the package and the devaluation, are switching to locally-produced cottonseed oil," Saulat Khan said. Demand for local sunflower, rapeseed and canola oils was also expected to rise. "The higher cost of imported vegoils will cut consumption," he added.
Edible oil imports fell 1.75 percent to 284,136 tonnes worth $153 million in July-September from 289,198 tonnes worth $237 million in the first quarter of 1995/96.
Vegoil imports shrank 18 percent to 1.142 million tonnes worth $855 million in 1995/96 from 1.394 million tonnes worth $997 million in 1994/95.
Palm oil imports dropped 14.72 percent to 984,000 tonnes in 1995/96 from 1.154 million tonnes in 1994/95. Soyoil imports were 34 percent down at 158,000 tonnes from 240,000 tonnes.

Dealer Abdul Majid said the government's latest economic measures had confused importers, who might need several weeks to assess their impact. "I think vegoil imports are likely to fall in the near future," he said.
Saulat Khan said Pakistan's production of canola, sunflower and rapeseed oils had risen slightly and was likely to exceed 200,000 tonnes, up from 150,000 tonnes in 1995/96.
